Last 15 minutes show roughly balanced flow: 9.0 SOL bought against 9.7 SOL sold, net -0.64 SOL, with 42 buyers versus 32 sellers. That is not a demand surge.

The rest of the brief argues against buying. It is classed OPERATOR: 702 SOL was bought in the first two minutes after graduation by 19 buyers, with the top 5 buyers taking 99.9% of that volume and a bundle share of 100%. Sell-to-buy in that window was 0.0002, meaning almost nothing was sold early, which reads as concentrated holding rather than organic interest. Demand here is operator-sourced, and its persistence depends on the operator's intent, which we cannot see.

Recommendation: no honest case for buying. Skip.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely loss is insider distribution. The operator profile fits: 702 SOL bought in the first two minutes from only 19 outside buyers, a top-5 buyer share of 99.87%, and a bundle share of 1.0 with top-3 at 1.0. Those insiders hold a large position that was bought cheap, and they have sold almost nothing so far (sell-to-buy ratio 0.0002). Their exit would hit a thin book: 799 SOL of pool depth against a $4.3M market cap.

The last 15 minutes show the trend is already turning: net flow is -0.64 SOL, 9.65 SOL sold against 9.01 bought, and 32 sellers against 42 buyers. A 0.19% return is effectively flat, and round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% would erase any small move. Operator-backed coins have been roughly break-even on average, so the edge is thin even before a dump.

Verdict: skip.
